transcript:
Header: Recorded 2026-09-30 15:00 PT | Duration 38m
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (Magnus CTO), Priya Singh (Magnus ML Eng), Marco Ruiz (Magnus SRE), Leah Park (Magnus Product)

00:00 Alice Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alice from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick round of intros?
00:08 Jordan Blake: Jordan here, CTO at Magnus. We build a developer-facing summarization API, looking to move away from hosted model provider due to cost.
00:15 Priya Singh: Priya, ML eng, mostly around model-inference and prompt pipelines.
00:20 Marco Ruiz: Marco, infra and SRE, I'll be focused on networking and security bits.
00:25 Ben Ortiz: Ben, SE at Redwood, I'll jump in on performance and POC specifics.
00:30 Alice Chen: Great. The goal today is to walk through our PLG quickstart — free credits, time-to-first-token, SDKs — and understand your success criteria, concurrency, and any regulatory constraints.

02:10 Jordan: High level, we want to validate cost per 1k tokens, latency at our median prompt length (~400 tokens), and whether Redwood Hosted will be enough or if we need Dedicated. We also need data never to persist in third-party storage for some endpoints.
02:38 Ben Ortiz: Got it. Typical questions: exact prompt mix, expected QPS, and tail latency SLOs. For quickstart we can give you a trial API key with credits to hit time-to-first-token in under an hour — people get tokens and example apps running fast.
03:15 Priya: How does the free credits redemption work? Is there any credit-card requirement?
03:25 Alice Chen: No card for the trial credits; we send a link to redeem credits tied to an account. SDKs (Python/Node) have example calls, streaming and embeddings samples. We'll also include a one-click Postman collection.
04:12 Marco: From infra POV, if we go Hosted that's fine for initial POC, but for production we need VPC/private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys. We also care about audit logs retention.
04:40 Ben Ortiz: Understood — Redwood Private and Redwood Dedicated both support VPC options. For Dedicated, you get reserved capacity and VPC, plus support for bringing your own KMS/HSM. For Private there's a customer-managed control plane option. We'll include SOC2 and ISO docs in the repo we send.
05:05 Jordan: Any performance benchmarks for median 400-token prompts? We're currently seeing 400-600ms 95th on another stack but at high cost.
05:20 Ben Ortiz: Benchmark depends on model selection and quantization. For a typical LLaMA-derived 13B on an A100-ish backend, you can see sub-400ms median token latencies with our runtime optimizations (KV cache, continuous batching). We'll share model-specific profiles. Note: hosted vs dedicated affects isolation and scheduling — Dedicated gives you more predictable tail latencies.

08:00 Leah Park: Quick question on the SDKs — is the streaming API compatible with our websocket infra?
08:12 Ben Ortiz: Yes, we support streaming over Server-Sent Events and websockets via the SDK. There are examples in the quickstart.

10:30 Priya: For embeddings/semantic search, do we get vector store recommendations? Any integration with FAISS/Chromadb?
10:40 Alice Chen: We provide embeddings APIs and a best-practices doc; we typically recommend Chromadb or FAISS and include example pipelines. We'll attach a short guide.

12:00 Marco: Security: SSO/SAML is required, RBAC + audit logs must be non-editable, and data residency in EU for some endpoints. Can Redwood accommodate?
12:20 Alice Chen: Yes — SAML SSO and RBAC are supported; audit logs are available and we can discuss retention windows. For EU residency, we can route requests and host within the region or consider Private deployment. We'll include the compliance pack.

15:00 Jordan: If we start with Hosted, how do we move to Dedicated later? Is there a migration path?
15:12 Ben Ortiz: Absolutely — same API surface. You can pin model versions and rollout config. Migration is mostly a config change plus capacity reservation. We can run a canary on Dedicated and fallback to Hosted if needed.

17:30 Priya: Pricing — what's the cost model? We need ballpark numbers for 1M tokens per month and for a Dedicated starter commit.
17:45 Alice Chen: Hosted is usage-based per token for generation/embeddings. We'll send a sample pricing calc for your prompt mix; Dedicated is monthly reserved GPU capacity and depends on the size of the commit. We'll include example math in the spreadsheet.

21:00 Marco: Networking nit: do you support private endpoints and VPC peering for Dedicated? Any Terraform modules?
21:15 Ben Ortiz: Yes to private endpoints and VPC peering. We have Terraform examples for most cloud providers; we'll attach them.

24:00 Jordan: Concern: latency variability with shared hosted pools during peak. How severe is burst contention?
24:20 Ben Ortiz: We mitigate burst contention with smart routing and autoscaling but shared pools can have more variability. Dedicated gives SLA-backed throughput/latency. For the trial, we'll recommend configuring a small burst buffer and measuring.

27:00 Priya: POC idea — can we run 50k tokens through the quickstart credits to measure cost/latency and then run the same on a Dedicated test rig?
27:10 Alice Chen: Yes, that's exactly what the free credits and quickstart are for. We'll provision a trial key and a sample workload template.

29:30 Marco: Any gotchas on KV cache or prefix caching for lower token spend?
29:42 Ben Ortiz: We'll show examples — prefix caching and automatic KV cache reuse can drop token counts significantly on conversational flows. It's part of Redwood Optimize recommendations.

32:00 Leah: Who will be our long-term contact?
32:05 Alice Chen: I'll be your AE and coordinate. Ben is your SE for technical follow-ups.

34:00 Jordan: Sounds good. Let's recap — we want trial API key, quickstart material, example pricing calc, and an SE latency estimate.
34:15 Alice Chen: Yep. Action items — we'll send the quickstart + credits link, Ben will run latency tests, Magnus to share prompts and infra constraints.

36:00 Ben Ortiz: Any other risks or blockers?
36:10 Priya: None on our side, just need those prompts and sample concurrency numbers.
36:20 Marco: I'll send network and SSO details.
36:30 Alice Chen: Great, we'll follow up by Friday. Thanks everyone.
36:40 Jordan: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "Redwood Dedied" appears), filler words, and speaker overlap in a couple places. Shared artifacts: quickstart guide link (link to /quickstart), pricing spreadsheet (link to /pricing/magnus-calc), SOC2 packet (link to /compliance/SOC2), Terraform VPC examples (link to /infra/terraform).
